questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the first Lok Sabha, the single largest party in the opposition was the Swatantra Party.
2. In the Lok Sabha, a "Leader of the Opposition" was recognised for the first time in 1969.
3. In the Lok Sabha, if a party does not have a minimum of 75 members, its leader cannot be recognised as the Leader of the Opposition.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The CPI (16 seats) was the largest opposition party in the first Lok Sabha. A Leader of the Opposition was first recognised in 1969, and the convention needs one-tenth of the House (55 seats), not 75. Only 2 is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q1

questions.q:
Which of the following leaf modifications occur(s) in the desert areas to inhibit water loss?
1. Hard and waxy leaves
2. Tiny leaves
3. Thorns instead of leaves
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Desert plants cut transpiration with waxy leaves, tiny leaves, and spines in place of leaves. All three are adaptations.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q2

questions.q:
As per the NSSO 70th Round "Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households", consider the following statements:
1. Rajasthan has the highest percentage share of agricultural households among its rural households.
2. Out of the total agricultural households in the country, a little over 60 percent belong to OBCs.
3. In Kerala, a little over 60 percent of agricultural households reported to have received maximum income from sources other than agricultural activities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The NSSO 70th round found Rajasthan with the highest share of agricultural households, and in Kerala most farm households earned mainly from non-farm sources. OBCs were about 45%, not over 60%.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q3

questions.q:
How is the National Green Tribunal (NGT) different from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)?
1. The NGT has been established by an Act whereas the CPCB has been created by an executive order of the Government.
2. The NGT provides environmental justice and helps reduce the burden of litigation in the higher courts whereas the CPCB promotes cleanliness of streams and wells, and aims to improve the quality of air in the country.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are statutory: the NGT under the NGT Act 2010 and the CPCB under the Water Act 1974, so 1 is wrong. Statement 2 correctly describes their roles.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Parliament of India can place a particular law in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution of India.
2. The validity of a law placed in the Ninth Schedule cannot be examined by any court and no judgement can be made on it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Parliament can place laws in the Ninth Schedule by amendment. But since I.R. Coelho (2007), laws added after 24 April 1973 can be reviewed for violating the basic structure, so 2 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q5

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes the term "Merchant Discount Rate" sometimes seen in news?
o: The incentive given by a bank to a merchant for accepting payments through debit cards pertaining to that bank.
The amount paid back by banks to their customers when they use debit cards for financial transactions for purchasing goods or services.
The charge to a merchant by a bank for accepting payments from his customers through the bank's debit cards.
The incentive given by the Government to merchants for promoting digital payments by their customers through Point of Sale (PoS) machines and debit cards.
questions.e: MDR is the fee a bank charges a merchant for accepting card payments, a percentage of each transaction.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q6

questions.q:
What is/are the consequence/consequences of a country becoming the member of the 'Nuclear Suppliers Group'?
1. It will have access to the latest and most efficient nuclear technologies.
2. It automatically becomes a member of "The Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT)".
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: NSG members get easier access to nuclear trade and technology. The NSG is not a treaty, and joining it does not make a country an NPT party.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q7

questions.q:
With reference to India's decision to levy an equalization tax of 6% on online advertisement services offered by non-resident entities, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is introduced as a part of the Income Tax Act.
2. Non-resident entities that offer advertisement services in India can claim a tax credit in their home country under the "Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements".
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The 6% equalisation levy was created under the Finance Act 2016, outside the Income Tax Act. Since it is not an income tax, foreign firms cannot claim treaty credit at home. Neither statement is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q8

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Review Committee Report has recommended a debt to GDP ratio of 60% for the general (combined) government by 2023, comprising 40% for the Central Government and 20% for the State Governments.
2. The Central Government has domestic liabilities of 21% of GDP as compared to that of 49% of GDP of the State Governments.
3. As per the Constitution of India, it is mandatory for a State to take the Central Government's consent for raising any loan if the former owes any outstanding liabilities to the latter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The FRBM Review Committee proposed a 60% general government debt target (Centre 40%, States 20%) by 2023. Statement 2 reverses the Centre and State figures. Article 293(3) requires Central consent for State loans while dues to the Centre are outstanding.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q9

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The quantity of imported edible oils is more than the domestic production of edible oils in the last five years.
2. The Government does not impose any customs duty on all the imported edible oils as a special case.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: India imports more edible oil than it produces. Imports are not duty-free; in 2018 the duty on crude edible oil was raised to 30%.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q10

questions.q: He wrote biographies of Mazzini, Garibaldi, Shivaji and Shrikrishna; stayed in America for some time; and was also elected to the Central Assembly. He was
questions.e: Lala Lajpat Rai wrote biographies of Mazzini, Garibaldi, Shivaji and Krishna, lived in the USA (founding the Home Rule League of America), and was elected to the Central Legislative Assembly.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q11

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Aadhaar card can be used as a proof of citizenship or domicile.
2. Once issued, Aadhaar number cannot be deactivated or omitted by the Issuing Authority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Under the Aadhaar Act, Aadhaar is not proof of citizenship or domicile, and UIDAI can omit or deactivate numbers. Neither statement is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q12

questions.q:
Which of the following has/have shrunk immensely/dried up in the recent past due to human activities?
1. Aral Sea
2. Black Sea
3. Lake Baikal
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Aral Sea shrank drastically after its feeder rivers were diverted for Soviet cotton irrigation. The Black Sea and Lake Baikal have not.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q13

questions.q: "Rule of Law Index" is released by which of the following?
o: The Office of UN Commissioner for Human Rights
questions.e: The Rule of Law Index is published by the World Justice Project, an independent organisation in Washington DC.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q14

questions.q: Which one of the following links all the ATMs in India?
questions.e: NPCI runs the National Financial Switch, the network linking all ATMs in India.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q15

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) is the amount that banks have to maintain in the form of their own funds to offset any loss that banks incur if the account-holders fail to repay dues.
2. CAR is decided by each individual bank.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: CAR is the bank's own capital held against risk-weighted assets to absorb losses. The minimum is set by the RBI under Basel norms, not by each bank.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q16

questions.q:
The identity platform 'Aadhaar' provides open "Application Programming Interfaces (APIs)". What does it imply?
1. It can be integrated into any electronic device.
2. Online authentication using iris is possible.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Open APIs let any device or software connect to Aadhaar using a standard format, and authentication can use fingerprint or iris. Both are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q17

questions.q: Very recently, in which of the following countries have lakhs of people either suffered from severe famine/acute malnutrition or died due to starvation caused by war/ethnic conflicts?
questions.e: In 2017 famine was declared in parts of South Sudan, and war-torn Yemen faced acute food insecurity for millions.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q18

questions.q:
Regarding Wood's Dispatch, which of the following statements are true?
1. Grants-in-Aid system was introduced.
2. Establishment of universities was recommended.
3. English as a medium of instruction at all levels of education was recommended.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Wood's Despatch (1854) introduced grants-in-aid and led to universities in Calcutta, Bombay and Madras. It favoured vernaculars at school level, so 3 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q19

questions.q: With reference to the Parliament of India, which of the following Parliamentary Committees scrutinizes and reports to the House whether the powers to make regulations, rules, sub-rules, by-laws, etc. conferred by the Constitution or delegated by the Parliament are being properly exercised by the Executive within the scope of such delegation?
questions.e: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation checks whether the executive uses delegated rule-making powers within limits.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q20

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. As per the Right to Education (RTE) Act, to be eligible for appointment as a teacher in a State, a person would be required to possess the minimum qualification laid down by the concerned State Council of Teacher Education.
2. As per the RTE Act, for teaching primary classes, a candidate is required to pass a Teacher Eligibility Test conducted in accordance with the National Council of Teacher Education guidelines.
3. In India, more than 90% of teacher education institutions are directly under the State Governments.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Under the RTE Act, teacher qualifications are set by NCTE (the national authority), and teachers must pass a TET held under NCTE guidelines. Most teacher education institutions are private, so 3 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q21

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Tradition State
1. Chapchar Kut festival Mizoram
2. Khongjom Parba ballad Manipur
3. Thang-Ta dance Sikkim
Which of the pairs given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Chapchar Kut is a Mizo festival and Khongjom Parba a Manipuri ballad. Thang-Ta is a Manipuri martial art, not from Sikkim.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q22

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 replaced the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
2. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is under the charge of Director General of Health Services in the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The FSS Act 2006 replaced the 1954 Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. FSSAI is an independent statutory body with its own chairperson, not under the DGHS.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q23

questions.q: The term “two-state solution” is sometimes mentioned in the news in the context of the affairs of
questions.e: The two-state solution proposes independent Israel and Palestine living side by side.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q24

questions.q:
With reference to the provisions made under the National Food Security Act, 2013, consider the following statements:
1. The families coming under the category of ‘below poverty line (BPL)’ only are eligible to receive subsidised food grains.
2. The eldest woman in a household, of age 18 years or above, shall be the head of the household for the purpose of issuance of a ration card.
3. Pregnant women and lactating mothers are entitled to a ‘take-home ration’ of 1600 calories per day during pregnancy and for six months thereafter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Under NFSA the eldest woman (18+) is head of household for the ration card. Coverage is not limited to BPL, and the maternal take-home ration norm is 600 calories, not 1600. Only 2 is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q25

questions.q: India enacted The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999 in order to comply with the obligations to
questions.e: India enacted the GI Act 1999 to meet its obligations under the WTO's TRIPS Agreement.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q26

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In India, State Governments do not have the power to auction non-coal mines.
2. Andhra Pradesh and Jharkhand do not have gold mines.
3. Rajasthan has iron ore mines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Rajasthan has iron ore. State Governments do auction non-coal minerals, and both Andhra Pradesh and Jharkhand have gold deposits. Only 3 is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q27

questions.q:
With reference to digital payments, consider the following statements:
1. BHIM app allows the user to transfer money to anyone with a UPI-enabled bank account.
2. While a chip-pin debit card has four factors of authentication, BHIM app has only two factors of authentication.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: BHIM is a UPI app for transfers to any UPI-enabled account. A chip-and-PIN card does not have four factors; BHIM uses two. Only 1 is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q28

questions.q: Among the following cities, which one lies on a longitude closest to that of Delhi?
questions.e: Delhi is at about 77.2°E and Bengaluru at about 77.6°E, the closest of the four.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q29

questions.q: International Labour Organization’s Conventions 138 and 182 are related to
o: Adaptation of agricultural practices to global climate change
Regulation of food prices and food security
questions.e: ILO Convention 138 sets the minimum age for employment and Convention 182 bans the worst forms of child labour.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q30

questions.q: Regarding Money Bill, which of the following statements is not correct?
o: A bill shall be deemed to be a Money Bill if it contains only provisions relating to imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax.
A Money Bill has provisions for the custody of the Consolidated Fund of India or the Contingency Fund of India.
A Money Bill is concerned with the appropriation of moneys out of the Contingency Fund of India.
A Money Bill deals with the regulation of borrowing of money or giving of any guarantee by the Government of India.
questions.e: Article 110 covers appropriation from the Consolidated Fund of India, not the Contingency Fund. So (c) is the incorrect statement.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q31

questions.q:
With reference to the election of the President of India, consider the following statements:
1. The value of the vote of each MLA varies from State to State.
2. The value of the vote of MPs of the Lok Sabha is more than the value of the vote of MPs of the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: An MLA's vote value depends on the state's population, so it varies. All elected MPs of both Houses have the same vote value. Only 1 is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q32

questions.q: In the Indian context, what is the implication of ratifying the ‘Additional Protocol’ with the ‘International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)’?
o: The civilian nuclear reactors come under IAEA safeguards.
The military nuclear installations come under the inspection of IAEA.
The country will have the privilege to buy uranium from the Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG).
The country automatically becomes a member of the NSG.
questions.e: India's Additional Protocol relates to its India-specific safeguards agreement covering civilian nuclear facilities, which stay under IAEA safeguards. Military facilities are excluded.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q33

questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Australia
2. Canada
3. China
4. India
5. Japan
6. USA
Which of the above are among the ‘free-trade partners’ of ASEAN?
questions.e: ASEAN's FTA partners were Australia (with New Zealand), China, India, Japan and South Korea. Canada and the USA were not.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q34

questions.q:
With reference to the ‘Global Alliance for Climate-Smart Agriculture (GACSA)’, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. GACSA is an outcome of the Climate Summit held in Paris in 2015.
2. Membership of GACSA does not create any binding obligations.
3. India was instrumental in the creation of GACSA.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: GACSA was launched at the UN Climate Summit in New York in 2014, not Paris 2015, and India was not a founder. Membership creates no binding obligations.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q35

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are the aim/aims of “Digital India” Plan of the Government of India?
1. Formation of India’s own Internet companies like China did.
2. Establish a policy framework to encourage overseas multinational corporations that collect Big Data to build their large data centres within our national geographical boundaries.
3. Connect many of our villages to the Internet and bring Wi-Fi to many of our schools, public places and major tourist centres.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Digital India aims at digital infrastructure such as broadband to villages and Wi-Fi in public places. Building Chinese-style internet firms or forcing data centres is not among its aims.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q36

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Towns sometimes mentioned in news Country
1. Aleppo Syria
2. Kirkuk Yemen
3. Mosul Palestine
4. Mazar-i-sharif Afghanistan
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Aleppo is in Syria and Mazar-i-Sharif in Afghanistan. Kirkuk and Mosul are both in Iraq.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q37

questions.q: In the Federation established by The Government of India Act of 1935, residuary powers were given to the
questions.e: Under the 1935 Act residuary powers lay with the Governor-General, who could authorise either legislature to legislate on them.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q38

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly shall vacate his/her office if he/she ceases to be a member of the Assembly.
2. Whenever the Legislative Assembly is dissolved, the Speaker shall vacate his/her office immediately.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: A Speaker vacates office on ceasing to be a member, but on dissolution continues until the new Assembly first meets (Article 179). Only 1 is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q39

questions.q: Which one of the following reflects the most appropriate relationship between law and liberty?
o: If there are more laws, there is less liberty.
If there are no laws, there is no liberty.
If there is liberty, laws have to be made by the people.
If laws are changed too often, liberty is in danger.
questions.e: Without law no one's freedom is protected from others, so there can be no real liberty. Law restrains harmful acts and secures liberty for all.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q40

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. No criminal proceedings shall be instituted against the Governor of a State in any court during his term of office.
2. The emoluments and allowances of the Governor of a State shall not be diminished during his term of office.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Article 361 bars criminal proceedings against a Governor during the term, and Article 158 bars reducing emoluments during the term. Both are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q41

questions.q: The well-known painting "Bani Thani" belongs to the
questions.e: Bani Thani, painted by Nihal Chand under Raja Sawant Singh, is the best-known work of the Kishangarh school.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q42

questions.q: What is “Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD)”, sometimes seen in the news?
o: A defence collaboration between Japan and South Korea
questions.e: THAAD is a US anti-ballistic missile system that destroys missiles in their final phase.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q43

questions.q:
With reference to cultural history of India, consider the following statements:
1. Most of the Tyagaraja Kritis are devotional songs in praise of Lord Krishna.
2. Tyagaraja created several new ragas.
3. Annamacharya and Tyagaraja are contemporaries.
4. Annamacharya kirtanas are devotional songs in praise of Lord Venkateshwara.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Tyagaraja composed new ragas, and Annamacharya's kirtanas praise Lord Venkateswara. Most Tyagaraja kritis praise Rama, and the two lived about three centuries apart.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q44

questions.q:
Which of the following are regarded as the main features of the "Rule of Law"?
1. Limitation of powers
2. Equality before law
3. People's responsibility to the Government
4. Liberty and civil rights
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Rule of law means limited power, equality before law and protection of liberty and rights. It does not make people responsible to the government.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q45

questions.q: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the meaning of legal tender money?
o: The money which is tendered in courts of law to defray the fee of legal cases
The money which a creditor is under compulsion to accept in settlement of his claims
The bank money in the form of cheques, drafts, bills of exchange, etc.
The metallic money in circulation in a country
questions.e: Legal tender is money that a creditor is legally bound to accept in settlement of a debt, such as RBI notes and coins.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q46

questions.q: If a commodity is provided free to the public by the Government, then
o: the opportunity cost is transferred from the consumers of the product to the tax-paying public.
the opportunity cost is transferred from the consumers of the product to the Government.
questions.e: Free provision does not remove the cost; it is paid from the government budget, so the burden shifts from users to taxpayers.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q47

questions.q: Increase in absolute and per capita real GNP do not connote a higher level of economic development, if
o: industrial output fails to keep pace with agricultural output.
agricultural output fails to keep pace with industrial output.
questions.e: Development means wider well-being. If poverty and unemployment rise, higher GNP does not mean higher development.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q48

questions.q:
Consider the following statements: Human capital formation as a concept is better explained in terms of a process which enables
1. individuals of a country to accumulate more capital.
2. increasing the knowledge, skill levels and capacities of the people of the country.
3. accumulation of tangible wealth.
4. accumulation of intangible wealth.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Human capital formation raises people's knowledge, skills and capacities, which is intangible wealth. So 2 and 4.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q49

questions.q: Despite being a high saving economy, capital formation may not result in significant increase in output due to
questions.e: A high capital-output ratio means each extra unit of output needs a lot of capital, so high saving yields little growth.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q50

questions.q:
After the Santhal Uprising subsided, what was/were the measure/measures taken by the colonial government?
1. The territories called 'Santhal Paraganas' were created.
2. It became illegal for a Santhal to transfer land to a non-Santhal.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: After the 1855-56 Santhal rebellion the British created the Santhal Parganas and barred transfer of Santhal land to outsiders. Both are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q51

questions.q: Economically, one of the results of the British rule in India in the 19th century was the
o: increase in the export of Indian handicrafts
growth in the number of Indian owned factories
rapid increase in the urban population
questions.e: British rule pushed farmers towards cash crops for the market and export, commercialising agriculture, while handicrafts declined.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q52

questions.q: If the President of India exercises his power as provided under Article 356 of the Constitution in respect of a particular State, then
o: the Assembly of the State is automatically dissolved.
the powers of the Legislature of that State shall be exercisable by or under the authority of the Parliament.
Article 19 is suspended in that State.
the President can make laws relating to that State.
questions.e: Under Article 356 the President can declare that the State Legislature's powers will be exercised by or under Parliament. The Assembly need not be dissolved.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q53

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Craft Heritage of
1. Puthukkuli shawls Tamil Nadu
2. Sujni embroidery Maharashtra
3. Uppada Jamdani saris Karnataka
Which of the pairs given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Puthukkuli shawls (Toda embroidery) belong to Tamil Nadu. Sujni embroidery is from Bihar and Uppada Jamdani saris from Andhra Pradesh.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q54

questions.q:
In which of the following areas can GPS technology be used?
1. Mobile phone operations
2. Banking operations
3. Controlling the power grids
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: GPS provides precise time signals used to synchronise mobile networks, banking systems and power grids, besides location. All three are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q55

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Reserve Bank of India manages and services Government of India Securities but not any State Government Securities.
2. Treasury bills are issued by the Government of India and there are no treasury bills issued by the State Governments.
3. Treasury bills offer are issued at a discount from the par value.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only the Centre issues treasury bills, at a discount to face value. The RBI also manages State Government securities, so 1 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q56

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Earth's magnetic field has reversed every few hundred thousand years.
2. When the Earth was created more than 4000 million years ago, there was 54% oxygen and no carbon dioxide.
3. When living organisms originated, they modified the early atmosphere of the Earth.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Earth's magnetic field has reversed many times, and early life (photosynthesis) changed the atmosphere. The early atmosphere had CO₂ and little oxygen, so 2 is false.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q57

questions.q: The terms ‘WannaCry, Petya and EternalBlue’ sometimes mentioned in the news recently are related to
questions.e: WannaCry and Petya were 2017 ransomware attacks that spread using the EternalBlue Windows exploit.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q58

questions.q:
With reference to the circumstances in Indian agriculture, the concept of “Conservation Agriculture” assumes significance. Which of the following fall under the Conservation Agriculture?
1. Avoiding the monoculture practices
2. Adopting minimum tillage
3. Avoiding the cultivation of plantation crops
4. Using crop residues to cover soil surface
5. Adopting spatial and temporal crop sequencing/crop rotations
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Conservation agriculture rests on minimum tillage, permanent soil cover with residues, and crop rotation. Avoiding plantation crops is not part of it.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q59

questions.q: The term "sixth mass extinction/sixth extinction" is often mentioned in the news in the context of the discussion of
o: Widespread monoculture practices in agriculture and large-scale commercial farming with indiscriminate use of chemicals in many parts of the world that may result in the loss of good native ecosystems.

Fears of a possible collision of a meteorite with the Earth in the near future in the manner it happened 65 million years ago that caused the mass extinction of many species including those of dinosaurs.

Large scale cultivation of genetically modified crops in many parts of the world and promoting their cultivation in other parts of the world which may cause the disappearance of good native crop plants and the loss of food biodiversity.
Mankind's over-exploitation/misuse of natural resources, fragmentation/loss of natural habitats, destruction of ecosystems, pollution and global climate change.
questions.e: The sixth extinction is the current rapid loss of species driven by human activity: habitat loss, over-exploitation, pollution and climate change.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q60

questions.q:
With reference to the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS), consider the following statements:
1. IRNSS has three satellites in geostationary and four satellites in geosynchronous orbits.
2. IRNSS covers entire India and about 5500 sq. km beyond its borders.
3. India will have its own satellite navigation system with full global coverage by the middle of 2019.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: IRNSS (NavIC) has three geostationary and four geosynchronous satellites. It covers India and about 1,500 km around it, and is regional, not global.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q61

questions.q:
Consider the following phenomena:
1. Light is affected by gravity.
2. The Universe is constantly expanding.
3. Matter warps its surrounding space-time.
Which of the above is/are the prediction/predictions of Albert Einstein's General Theory of Relativity, often discussed in media?
questions.e: General Relativity treats gravity as curvature of space-time by matter, which bends light, and its equations predict an expanding Universe. All three are predictions.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q62

questions.q:
With reference to the Genetically Modified mustard (GM mustard) developed in India, consider the following statements:
1. GM mustard has the genes of a soil bacterium that give the plant the property of pest-resistance to a wide variety of pests.
2. GM mustard has the genes that allow the plant cross-pollination and hybridization.
3. GM mustard has been developed jointly by the IARI and Punjab Agricultural University.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: GM mustard DMH-11 uses barnase-barstar genes for a pollination-control system enabling hybrid seed. It was developed at Delhi University and is not pest-resistant.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q63

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Terms sometimes seen in news Context/Topic
1. Belle II experiment Artificial Intelligence
2. Blockchain technology Digital/Cryptocurrency
3. CRISPR – Cas9 Particle Physics
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.e: Blockchain underlies cryptocurrencies. Belle II is a particle physics experiment and CRISPR-Cas9 is a gene-editing tool.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q64

questions.q: Which of the following statements best describes "carbon fertilization"?
o: Increased plant growth due to increased concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere
Increased temperature of Earth due to increased concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere
Increased acidity of oceans as a result of increased concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere
Adaptation of all living beings on Earth to the climate change brought about by the increased concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere
questions.e: Carbon fertilisation is increased plant growth due to higher CO₂ in the air.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q65

questions.q: When the alarm of your smartphone rings in the morning, you wake up and tap it to stop the alarm which causes your geyser to be switched on automatically. The smart mirror in your bathroom shows the day’s weather and also indicates the level of water in your overhead tank. After you take some groceries from your refrigerator for making breakfast, it recognises the shortage of stock in it and places an order for the supply of fresh grocery items. When you step out of your house and lock the door, all lights, fans, geysers and AC machines get switched off automatically. On your way to office, your car warns you about traffic congestion ahead and suggests an alternative route, and if you are late for a meeting, it sends a message to your office accordingly. In the context of emerging communication technologies, which one of the following terms best applies to the above scenario?
questions.e: Everyday devices talking to each other over the internet and acting on their own is the Internet of Things.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q66

questions.q:
With reference to solar power production in India, consider the following statements:
1. India is the third largest in the world in the manufacture of silicon wafers used in photovoltaic units.
2. The solar power tariffs are determined by the Solar Energy Corporation of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: India imports most silicon wafers, and solar tariffs are discovered through competitive bidding, not fixed by SECI. Neither is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q67

questions.q: The staple commodities of export by the English East India Company from Bengal in the middle of the 18th century were
o: Copper, silver, gold, spices and tea
questions.e: The Company's main exports from Bengal were cotton and silk textiles, saltpetre and opium.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q68

questions.q: Which one of the following is a very significant aspect of the Champaran Satyagraha?
o: Active all-India participation of lawyers, students and women in the National Movement
Active involvement of Dalit and Tribal communities of India in the National Movement
Joining of peasant unrest to India's National Movement
Drastic decrease in the cultivation of plantation crops and commercial crops
questions.e: Champaran (1917) linked the grievances of indigo peasants to the national movement under Gandhi.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q69

questions.q: Who among the following were the founders of the “Hind Mazdoor Sabha” established in 1948?
o: B. Krishna Pillai, E.M.S. Namboodiripad and K.C. George
Jayaprakash Narayan, Deen Dayal Upadhyay and M.N. Roy
C.P. Ramaswamy Iyer, K. Kamaraj and Veeresalingam Pantulu
Ashok Mehta, T.S. Ramanujam and G.G. Mehta
questions.e: The Hind Mazdoor Sabha was founded in 1948 by socialists including Ashok Mehta, T.S. Ramanujam and G.G. Mehta.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q70

questions.q: With reference to the religious practices in India, the “Sthanakvasi” sect belongs to
questions.e: Sthanakvasis are a Svetambara Jain sect that rejects idol worship and prays in halls (sthanaks).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q71

questions.q:
With reference to the cultural history of India, consider the following statements:
1. White marble was used in making Buland Darwaza and Khankah at Fatehpur Sikri.
2. Red sandstone and marble were used in making Bara Imambara and Rumi Darwaza at Lucknow.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Fatehpur Sikri's buildings are mainly red sandstone, and Lucknow's Bara Imambara and Rumi Darwaza are of brick and lime plaster. Neither statement is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q72

questions.q: Which one of the following foreign travellers elaborately discussed about diamonds and diamond mines of India?
questions.e: The French jeweller Jean-Baptiste Tavernier described India's diamond mines in detail in his travels.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q73

questions.q: With reference to Indian history, who among the following is a future Buddha, yet to come to save the world?
questions.e: Maitreya is the future Buddha in Buddhist tradition. Avalokiteshvara (Padmapani, Lokeshvara) is a bodhisattva of compassion.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q74

questions.q: Which one of the following statements does not apply to the system of Subsidiary Alliance introduced by Lord Wellesley?
o: To maintain a large standing army at other's expense
To keep India safe from Napoleonic danger
To secure a fixed income for the Company
To establish British paramountcy over the Indian States
questions.e: Subsidiary alliances made Indian rulers pay for British troops, protected against French influence and established British paramountcy. A fixed income for the Company was not the aim.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q75

questions.q:
Which of the following led to the introduction of English Education in India?
1. Charter Act of 1813
2. General Committee of Public Instruction, 1823
3. Orientalist and Anglicist Controversy
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Charter Act 1813 set aside money for education, the 1823 Committee of Public Instruction managed it, and the Orientalist-Anglicist debate led to Macaulay's Minute (1835). All three led to English education.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q76

questions.q: Which one of the following is an artificial lake?
questions.e: Kodaikanal Lake is man-made, created in 1863. Kolleru, Nainital and Renuka are natural lakes.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q77

questions.q:
With reference to Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, consider the following statements:
1. It is the flagship scheme of the Ministry of Labour and Employment.
2. It, among other things, will also impart training in soft skills, entrepreneurship, financial and digital literacy.
3. It aims to align the competencies of the unregulated workforce of the country to the National Skill Qualification Framework.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: PMKVY is under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, not Labour. It trains in soft skills, entrepreneurship and literacy, and aligns skills with NSQF.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q78

questions.q: In 1920, which of the following changed its name to “Swarajya Sabha”?
questions.e: In 1920 the All India Home Rule League renamed itself Swarajya Sabha.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q79

questions.q: Which among the following events happened earliest?
o: Satyendranath Tagore became the first Indian to succeed in the Indian Civil Services Examination.
questions.e: Neel Darpan was written in 1860, before Satyendranath Tagore's ICS (1863), the Arya Samaj (1875) and Anandmath (1882).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q80

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are the possible consequence/s of heavy sand mining in riverbeds?
1. Decreased salinity in the river
2. Pollution of groundwater
3. Lowering of the water-table
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Heavy sand mining can pollute groundwater and lower the water table. It tends to increase salinity near coasts, not decrease it.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q81

questions.q:
With reference to agricultural soils, consider the following statements:
1. A high content of organic matter in soil drastically reduces its water holding capacity.
2. Soil does not play any role in the sulphur cycle.
3. Irrigation over a period of time can contribute to the salinization of some agricultural lands.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Long irrigation can salinise soil. Organic matter increases water-holding capacity, and soil is central to the sulphur cycle.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q82

questions.q: The Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE), a UN mechanism to assist countries transition towards greener and more inclusive economies, emerged at
o: The Earth Summit on Sustainable Development 2002, Johannesburg
The United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development 2012, Rio de Janeiro
The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change 2015, Paris
The World Sustainable Development Summit 2016, New Delhi
questions.e: PAGE was launched in 2013 in response to the call at Rio+20 (2012) for help with green economy transitions.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q83

questions.q:
“3D printing” has applications in which of the following?
1. Preparation of confectionery items
2. Manufacture of bionic ears
3. Automotive industry
4. Reconstructive surgeries
5. Data processing technologies
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: 3D printing has been used for confectionery, bionic ears, auto parts, reconstructive implants and electronics. All five apply.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q84

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Barren Island volcano is an active volcano located in the Indian territory.
2. Barren Island lies about 140 km east of Great Nicobar.
3. The last time the Barren Island volcano erupted was in 1991 and it has remained inactive since then.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Barren Island is India's only active volcano. It lies north-east of Port Blair, not east of Great Nicobar, and has erupted since 1991.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q85

questions.q: Why is a plant called Prosopis juliflora often mentioned in news?
o: Its extract is widely used in cosmetics.
It tends to reduce the biodiversity in the area in which it grows.
Its extract is used in the synthesis of pesticides.
questions.e: Prosopis juliflora is an invasive tree that crowds out native plants and reduces biodiversity.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q86

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Most of the world’s coral reefs are in tropical waters.
2. More than one-third of the world’s coral reefs are located in the territories of Australia, Indonesia and Philippines.
3. Coral reefs host far more number of animal phyla than those hosted by tropical rainforests.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Most reefs are in tropical waters; Australia, Indonesia and the Philippines hold over a third of them; and reefs host more animal phyla than rainforests. All three are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q87

questions.q: “Momentum for Change: Climate Neutral Now” is an initiative launched by
o: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
questions.e: Climate Neutral Now was launched in 2015 by the UNFCCC Secretariat.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q88

questions.q:
With reference to educational institutions during colonial rule in India, consider the following pairs: Institution Founder
1. Sanskrit College at Benaras William Jones
2. Calcutta Madarsa Warren Hastings
3. Fort William College Arthur Wellesley
Which of the pairs given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Warren Hastings founded the Calcutta Madrasa (1781). Jonathan Duncan founded the Benaras Sanskrit College and Lord (Richard) Wellesley Fort William College.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q89

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Regions sometimes mentioned in news Country
1. Catalonia Spain
2. Crimea Hungary
3. Mindanao Philippines
4. Oromia Nigeria
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Catalonia is in Spain and Mindanao in the Philippines. Crimea belongs to Ukraine and Oromia is in Ethiopia.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q90

questions.q:
Consider the following events:
1. The first democratically elected communist party government formed in a State in India.
2. India’s then largest bank, ‘Imperial Bank of India’, was renamed ‘State Bank of India’.
3. Air India was nationalised and became the national carrier.
4. Goa became a part of independent India.
Which of the following is the correct chronological sequence of the above events?
questions.e: Air India nationalised 1953, SBI formed 1955, Kerala communist government 1957, Goa joined India 1961: 3-2-1-4.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q91

questions.q: Right to Privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of Right to Life and Personal Liberty. Which of the following in the Constitution of India correctly and appropriately imply the above statement?
o: Article 14 and the provisions under the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution
Article 17 and the Directive Principles of State Policy in Part IV
Article 21 and the freedoms guaranteed in Part III
Article 24 and the provisions under the 44th Amendment to the Constitution
questions.e: The Puttaswamy judgment (2017) held privacy to be part of Article 21 and the freedoms in Part III.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q92

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Areca nut
2. Barley
3. Coffee
4. Finger millet
5. Groundnut
6. Sesamum
7. Turmeric The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has announced the Minimum Support Price for which of the above?
questions.e: MSP covers barley, ragi, groundnut and sesamum. Areca nut, coffee and turmeric have no MSP.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q93

questions.q: In which one of the following States is Pakhui Wildlife Sanctuary located?
questions.e: Pakhui (Pakke) Wildlife Sanctuary and Tiger Reserve is in East Kameng district, Arunachal Pradesh.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q94

questions.q:
With reference to India’s satellite launch vehicles, consider the following statements:
1. PSLVs launch the satellites useful for Earth resources monitoring whereas GSLVs are designed mainly to launch communication satellites.
2. Satellites launched by PSLV appear to remain permanently fixed in the same position in the sky, as viewed from a particular location on Earth.
3. GSLV Mk III is a four-staged launch vehicle with the first and third stages using solid rocket motors; and the second and fourth stages using liquid rocket engines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: PSLV launches earth-observation satellites and GSLV mainly communication satellites. PSLV satellites are not geostationary, and GSLV Mk III has three stages. Only 1 is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q95

questions.q:
With reference to the governance of public sector banking in India, consider the following statements:
1. Capital infusion into public sector banks by the Government of India has steadily increased in the last decade.
2. To put the public sector banks in order, the merger of associate banks with the parent State Bank of India has been affected.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: SBI's associate banks were merged with it in 2017. Capital infusion into PSBs did not rise steadily, so 1 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q96

questions.q:
Consider the following items:
1. Cereal grains hulled
2. Chicken eggs cooked
3. Fish processed and canned
4. Newspapers containing advertising material
Which of the above items is/are exempted under GST (Goods and Services Tax)?
questions.e: Hulled cereal grains, cooked eggs and newspapers are GST-exempt; processed and canned fish is taxed.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q97

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The definition of “Critical Wildlife Habitat” is incorporated in the Forest Rights Act, 2006.
2. For the first time in India, Baigas have been given Habitat Rights.
3. Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change officially decides and declares Habitat Rights for Primitive and Vulnerable Tribal Groups in any part of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Forest Rights Act defines critical wildlife habitat, and the Baigas were the first to get habitat rights (2015). Habitat rights are recognised through the Gram Sabha process, not declared by the Environment Ministry.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q98

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Birds
2. Dust blowing
3. Rain
4. Wind blowing
Which of the above spread plant diseases?
questions.e: Plant pathogens are carried by birds, dust, rain splash and wind. All four spread disease.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q99

questions.q:
With reference to organic farming in India, consider the following statements:
1. ‘The National Programme for Organic Production’ (NPOP) is operated under the guidelines and directions of the Union Ministry of Rural Development.
2. ‘The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority’ (APEDA) functions as the Secretariat for the implementation of NPOP.
3. Sikkim has become India’s first fully organic State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: NPOP is run by the Commerce Ministry with APEDA as secretariat, not by Rural Development. Sikkim became India's first fully organic state in 2016.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2018, GS Paper I, Q100
